issues.description: Interface naming mismatch: the problem statement and template expect an interface named 'Rideable' with method messageOnRide() (problem_statement.md references at lines 47-53 and 62-64; template Main.java uses Rideable at line 23). The solution repository instead provides an interface named 'Mountable' that declares messageOnRide() (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Mountable.java) and has Pig and Seal implement Mountable (Pig.java implements Mountable at line 3; Seal.java implements Mountable at line 4). Meanwhile src/de/tum/cit/ase/Rideable.java in the solution is empty. This name/file mismatch (Rideable vs Mountable, plus an empty Rideable.java) breaks the one-to-one mapping between the exercise description/template and the provided solution, will confuse students about which interface to implement, and can cause compilation or test failures if tests or template code refer to Rideable.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the interface name across all artifacts. Preferred fixes: (A) Rename Mountable.java to Rideable.java (or make Mountable a simple alias) and update Pig.java and Seal.java to implement Rideable; replace or remove the empty Rideable.java so it contains the declaration: public interface Rideable { String messageOnRide(); } OR (B) If Mountable is intentionally preferred, update the problem statement and template to refer to Mountable instead of Rideable. Ensure the final Rideable/Mountable interface declares messageOnRide() with the expected signature and that all references (problem text, template, solution, and tests) use the same identifier.
